# The current thread

Its identifier, giving way to other threads, and how many can run at once.

<h2 id="current-id"><code>CurrentId</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CurrentId() -> uint64
```

The calling thread's system-wide identifier.
No two live threads share one, but the system may give a finished thread's identifier to a new thread.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Current.rux#L9)

**Returns**: the identifier

<h2 id="yield"><code>Yield</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Yield()
```

Offers the processor to another thread that is ready to run, and returns when this one is scheduled again.
A hint for code that waits on another thread, not a way to order threads.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Current.rux#L16)

<h2 id="available-parallelism"><code>AvailableParallelism</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AvailableParallelism() -> uint
```

How many threads can usefully run at once: the number of processors online, and at least one.
The answer can change while a program runs, as processors go online or offline.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Current.rux#L24)

**Returns**: the number of processors, never zero
